criteria.name: Introduction — Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design; discusses the context of ethical issues in engineering organisations; identifies relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues.
criteria.reasoning: The introduction articulates three distinct ethical issues in engineering design, distinguishing between commercial cadence and risk-based testing. It demonstrates an exceptional understanding of organisational context and stakeholder interests via a thorough stakeholder matrix in Table 1.

evidence.quote: Three ethical issues follow. First, test coverage is being set by the release calendar instead of by risk

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions on the ethical issues; draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.
criteria.reasoning: The report constructs deeply balanced, objective arguments for and against shipping, dissecting both commercial and safety realities. It synthesises these arguments into clear, actionable decision-making recommendations for five distinct stakeholder groups.

evidence.quote: Company management should fund the skipped tests for this contract, disclose the measured failure rates to the health department

criteria.name: Compelling Argument that supports conclusion — The report forms a compelling argument that justifies the conclusion; the body follows a logical structure, with linked paragraphs and content ordered to support the argument; arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders.
criteria.reasoning: The submission develops a rigorous, compelling argument that directly justifies its final recommendations. Paragraphs flow seamlessly from problem framing to comparative options analysis and actionable guidance, demonstrating a systematic understanding of stakeholder tensions.

evidence.quote: Options B and C respect every stakeholder's interests better than either extreme.

criteria.name: Research and Evidence — Arguments are substantiated with adequate references and qualitative/quantitative evidence; research demonstrates a balanced, in-depth understanding of the topic.
criteria.reasoning: Arguments are substantiated with authoritative references and both qualitative and quantitative evidence. The author integrates relevant external cases (WannaCry, Therac-25, Intel Pentium, and Volkswagen) alongside professional codes and risk management standards.

evidence.quote: at least 81 of 236 hospital trusts in England were disrupted, an estimated 19,000 appointments were cancelled

criteria.name: Report Structure, Format and Language — The report includes appropriate sections serving their functions (abstract, introduction, body, and conclusion); maps, figures, tables, and visual elements are correctly used to support discussion; writing is grammatically correct, fluent, concise, easy to read and understand, and uses appropriate word choice; references are well-structured and appropriate, supporting the report’s motivations.
criteria.reasoning: The report is structured and written with exceptional clarity and fluency. It integrates multiple visual elements competently (two structured comparison tables and an original decision flowchart) and employs consistent, professional IEEE referencing.

requirements.where: How should Rachel decide when to ship?

overall: An exemplary report that thoroughly analyses the ethical scenario with technical maturity, compelling logic, and authoritative real-world evidence. The multi-stakeholder recommendations and original decision-tree framework are outstanding.

feedback.summary: You delivered an outstanding report analyzing Rachel’s ethical dilemma with remarkable technical depth and critical balance. By pairing quantitative case evidence with clear frameworks—such as your stakeholder matrix and decision flowchart—you constructed a compelling, professional argument. You achieved the highest rubric band across all criteria. To further hone your engineering practice, focus on refining operational implementation plans and risk-mitigation timelines for your recommendations.
next_steps: Translate your decision flowchart into an actionable standard operating procedure that details specific quantitative testing thresholds and escalation protocols.
In future case evaluations, explore resource allocation models to detail how management can realistically fund deferred testing without jeopardizing delivery contracts.
Continue combining multidisciplinary case precedents (hardware, software, and organizational failures) to reinforce ethical risk assessments in safety-critical systems.

criteria.C1: You clearly articulated three ethical issues in the Introduction, linking them to engineering design alongside Table 1's stakeholder matrix. You achieved the Excellent tier by demonstrating an understanding of both organizational context and diverse stakeholder interests. To maintain this standard in future work, continue explicitly differentiating commercial pressures from risk-based engineering testing requirements.
criteria.C2: In your arguments for and against shipping and your Recommendations section, you constructed objective arguments addressing safety and commercial realities. Providing distinct recommendations for five stakeholder groups fulfilled the Excellent criteria. To sustain this level in future projects, continue presenting rigorous multi-perspective analyses before drawing stakeholder-specific conclusions.
criteria.C3: Your logical progression from problem framing to the options analysis in 'The Most Ethical Path' formed a compelling narrative that directly justified your recommendations, fulfilling the Excellent descriptor. To maintain this standard, continue structuring comparative options so that each proposed mitigation directly resolves previously identified stakeholder tensions and technical risks.
criteria.C4: You substantiated your claims exceptionally well by integrating quantitative data, professional standards, and case studies (Therac-25, WannaCry, Intel Pentium, Volkswagen) in 'Arguments against shipping'. This fulfilled the Excellent level for depth and balance. Maintain this quality by continuing to pair authoritative real-world precedents with numerical impact data.
criteria.C5: Your report was fluently written with professional IEEE referencing and effective visual elements, including your comparison tables and the original decision flowchart (Image 1). You achieved the Excellent level through clear language and competent visual integration. Continue applying this high standard of technical writing and visual communication in future reports.
